decision: KEEP TypeScript/native DOM composition after source-bound re-review; FIX the shared adapter withdrawal gate across display and connection lifetimes.
constraints: One explicitly requested, host-authorized read-only observation session; no view reads before start or after revocation. Synchronous local withdrawal must survive a failing adapter clear.
One locale owner for all observation, connection and contextual guidance. Native controls, offline bundled ESM, no account service, credentials, persistent state, new timer or server contract.
Single pending session through cleanup; explicit restart only. Preserve source freshness uncertainty and UNKNOWN current state.

Both lifecycle and connection controls may withdraw the same adapter. A synchronous adapter callback must not start a session while either withdrawal is in progress; recursive adapter clearing fails closed.

alternatives.assessment: Retained: typed native callbacks and AbortSignal interop with direct synchronous shared-source gating. Executed pageshow/resume regressions show why composition needs its own gate even when both child components have local gates. Types alone do not enforce runtime ordering.
Same native runtime and ordering are possible; annotations and public declarations remain necessary. No measured runtime advantage or stronger callback boundary has been established.

Official external function bindings make native host interoperation credible. The composition has no separate algebraic domain model; translating the same callbacks does not establish a material safety or interoperability gain.

Ports supply an explicit application/JavaScript boundary. Native session cancellation and synchronous source withdrawal would remain in JavaScript adapters; the additional message boundary does not eliminate this component obligation.

Reactive lifecycle and reusable custom elements are credible for broader UI systems. Asynchronous rendering cannot govern immediate withdrawal here; a separate synchronous gate would still be needed. There is no present custom-element requirement.

limits: setEnabled is a local display/request gate, not authentication or authorization. Trusted host and service enforce access; the adapter start promise covers reception and cleanup and must honor cancellation.
No cross-language benchmark or hard-real-time claim. Existing browser timer scheduling limits and independent device/accessibility/customer acceptance gates remain.
The optional panel/host locale-request callback delegates user language choice to a containing owner. Existing three-argument callers retain local selection.
This bounded client composition has contextual guidance but does not provide the complete P19 release-SHA-bound Help Center, role inventory, search, onboarding or installed customer distribution.
No targeting, weapon integration, physical actuation, identity histories or tactical/cryptographic/availability qualification.

Reviewed 2026-10-10 against official TypeScript, ReScript, Elm and Lit sources. These compare ecosystem interoperation and scheduling properties, not alternate-language benchmark results. Host callbacks remain trusted integration code.
